text:
marta: pushed initial bring-up numbers for draft-model-12b-quant to the shared bucket. quick summary: 1.8x token/s vs fp16 baseline on p4d; end-to-end median latency down ~12ms with speculative prefetch enabled. results + logs: gs://redwood-experiments/draft-onboard/7987654321/

hussein: nice. did you run with our two-stage speculative sampler or the simple prefetch?

marta: two-stage (fast candidate + late-stage fallback). config below. note: we saw a small quality dip on abstractive summarization holdout.

oliver: small = how small? numbers?

marta: ROUGE-L down 0.6 absolute, BLEU irrelevant for this set, human likert median -0.2. perplexity on eval set basically unchanged. implies degeneracy in rank ordering, not raw model calibration.

sara: can you paste the decode config and quant details? want to repro.

marta: ```
speculative: {
  enable: true,
  fast_sampler: {type: "top-k", k: 40, temp: 0.9},
  fallback_sampler: {type: "top-p", p: 0.95, temp: 1.0},
  fast_token_budget: 6
}
quant: {bits: 4, scheme: "q8_0_like", perchannel: true}
runtime: {batching: auto, kv_cache: prefix, max_seq: 2048}
```

aaron: thanks. did you test with and without KV warm-prefix? that can interact badly with speculative prefills.

marta: yeah — with KV warm-prefix enabled we get ~7-9% more token/s, but the quality dip persists. disabling warm-prefix reduces throughput but eliminates the ROUGE hit.

hussein: interesting. suggests prefetching stale KV entries causes misranked continuations for some prompts. any examples?

marta: pasted a couple of problematic prompts in the logs; short-context news-summary that starts with an ambiguous phrase. fast sampler picks a coherent short continuation that steers style away from reference; fallback would have corrected later but we return earlier tokens as final because of early commitment heuristic.

oliver: could be due to our early-commit threshold (p>0.7). If fast sampler output has high local token prob but lower global quality, early-commit gives it priority. worth testing stricter threshold + longer fast_token_budget.

sara: procedural ask: let's run a controlled A/B on the holdout with these arms: 1) baseline fp16, no speculative; 2) quant+no speculative; 3) quant+speculative (current); 4) quant+speculative with higher commit threshold (p>0.85) + warm-prefix off. keep batch/seq same.

marta: agreed. I'll queue those. planning to use 2k examples from our summarization holdout and 2k from the dialog-longform holdout. will collect automatic (ROUGE/ROUGE-L/CLIPScore) + 200 human likert triples per arm for the biggest diffs.

aaron: for the human eval, use blind pairwise with anchor examples and shuffle order per worker. also capture time-to-first-token latencies — product cares about that.

hussein: also add an exposure metric: fraction of tokens generated by fast sampler vs fallback. that will help correlate throughput gains with quality change.

marta: good call. i'll log an "exposure_ratio" per request (fast_tokens / total_tokens).

ci-bot: build 7987654321-spec-onboard started on infra-ci (matrix: p4d, quant=4bit, runtime=speculative). ETA ~45m.

oliver: another idea — try simpler fast_sampler hyper: greedy for first 2 tokens then top-k. sometimes the first few tokens determine style; greedy may anchor to stable start.

sara: and keep a holdout that measures recency-sensitive factuality (QA-style). spec-prefetch might hallucinate earlier if KV is from stale context. add an F1/QA metric.

marta: noted. i'll kick off the matrix: arms x seeds(3) x holdouts(2). will post updated artifacts when CI finishes.

hussein: if we see consistent ROUGE regression only on summarization but not on dialog, we probably need either fallback policy adjustments or a reranker on final beam. reranker could be expensive though.

oliver: quick hack: run a cheap ranker (embedding sim to prompt+context) on first 8 tokens generated by fast sampler; if similarity < threshold, prefer fallback. cheap and parallelizable.

marta: adding that to the experiment list as arm 5 (quant+speculative+cheap-rerank).

sara: timeline? product wants recommendation for Dedicated customers by EOW.

marta: CI results expected in ~50m. automated metrics in another 2h, human eval next 48h. will write interim note after automated run.

hussein: thanks — please tag me and put a short ops checklist for Dedicated rollout (limits, runtime flags, config presets). we should ship speculative as an opt-in with clear tradeoffs.

marta: will do. tagging final: @hussein. thanks team. :thumbsup:
